Verified against the 64 factory patches in your own corpus. Here's what's true:

**The ZOIA-facing name is the 16-byte field at offset 4 of the .bin, and the SD-card filename must match it.** Across all 64 files in `Tests/ZoiaCanvasTests/Corpus/FactoryEuroburo/`, the filename segment after `_zoia_` equals the internal name with spaces swapped for underscores — 64/64, zero mismatches. Max internal length observed: 15 chars.

```
000_zoia_slightlyrandom.bin   internal=[slightlyrandom]
006_zoia_Shim_Shim_Meree.bin  internal=[Shim Shim Meree]
011_zoia_Grains_de_folie.bin  internal=[Grains de folie]
```

So the rule is `NNN_zoia_Name_With_Underscores.bin` on the card, and the same string with spaces inside the binary. I did **not** verify which of the two the firmware actually reads for the menu — the corpus only proves they always agree, so write both and the question doesn't matter.

**Why you can't do it today:** nothing in the app ever sets `patchName`.

- [PatchDocument.swift:82](Sources/ZoiaCanvas/Model/PatchDocument.swift:82) initializes it to `"Untitled"`.
- [PatchSession.swift:114](Sources/ZoiaCanvas/PatchSession.swift:114) only adopts the filename `if document.patchName.isEmpty` — which is never true, because `"Untitled"` is not empty.
- No view edits it. `patchName` appears only in the window title at [ContentView.swift:89](Sources/ZoiaCanvas/ContentView.swift:89).

Net effect: every patch you build from scratch and save as `MyThing.bin` writes `Untitled` into the binary's name field, and the save panel proposes a filename with no `NNN_zoia_` prefix.

**On your original question** — that behavior already exists. [PatchSession.save()](Sources/ZoiaCanvas/PatchSession.swift:93) does `fileURL ?? runSavePanel(...)` with `adopt: true`, so ⌘S on a never-saved patch runs the panel and keeps that file open. The gap was never the Save As; it was that the name you type there doesn't reach the ZOIA.

## What the ZOIA reads

The 16-byte name field at offset 4 of the `.bin`. The SD-card filename repeats it as `NNN_zoia_<name>.bin` with **every non-alphanumeric character** written as an underscore. Verified against all 128 factory patches in your corpus, zero exceptions — including `Factory/017_zoia_V_Sync.bin`, whose header name is `V-Sync`.

That corrects what I said earlier: it isn't just spaces. It also means filename → name is lossy (an underscore could have been a space or a hyphen), which is why the header name is now the source of truth and the filename derives from it, never the reverse.

## What changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| [ZoiaPatch.swift](Sources/ZoiaCanvas/Format/ZoiaPatch.swift) | New `ZoiaPatchNaming`: 16-byte clamp, `fileName(for:slot:)`, slot parsing, lossy inverse |
| [PatchDocument.swift](Sources/ZoiaCanvas/Model/PatchDocument.swift) | `patchName` is now `private(set)` with `setPatchName` (marks edited) and `adoptPatchName` (doesn't) |
| [PatchSession.swift](Sources/ZoiaCanvas/PatchSession.swift) | Rename flow, save-panel accessory field, `save()` routes an unsaved patch through Save As |
| [ContentView.swift](Sources/ZoiaCanvas/ContentView.swift) | Title bar bound to the patch name; unsaved state moved to the close-button dot |
| [PatchLayoutStore.swift](Sources/ZoiaCanvas/Model/PatchLayoutStore.swift) | `discard(for:)` so a rename doesn't orphan the layout sidecar |

Behavior:
